identity.title: Establish durable MVVM and library ownership boundaries

origin.summary: The owner approved documenting and executing the repository-wide refactoring plan so View, ViewModel, Model, Command, Converter, Behavior, reusable libraries, documentation, and binary inputs have explicit durable owners.

state.current_summary: The original M1-M7 checkpoint evidence remains valid for its named extractions, but the 2026-08-19 whole-repository audit found broader MVVM criteria still unmet. PL-0026 supersedes the overbroad closure and owns the remaining View, ViewModel, smoke, Tool Lab, and verification-boundary work.

objective.summary: Refactor OpenVisionLab 3D Studio into explicit MVVM and reusable library ownership boundaries without changing observable inspection behavior or the public Viewer hosting contract.
constraints: Preserve explicit Preview, Publish, Run, Validation, source/result separation, stable identities, and no-execution presentation or restored-state actions.
Organize by stable feature and responsibility; do not split solely by line count or treat partial files as architecture.
Keep Core, Data, Tools, Runner, and Reporting runtime-neutral; keep WPF, SharpGL, docking, pointer, dialog, and Window operations in presentation adapters.
Preserve the public Viewer host and binary bundle compatibility through explicit compatibility seams.
Do not add a DI container, mediator, event bus, speculative interfaces, or one-project-per-feature structure.
Keep active vendored packages as packages; create lib only for a future unavoidable loose-DLL dependency with license, provenance, and SHA-256 records.
Preserve the existing PL-0024 dirty worktree and do not commit or push without separate authorization.

criteria.text: Shell and Viewer use a shared Presentation command implementation while the old Viewer public command surface remains compatible and Shell no longer imports it as its command owner.
Shell and Runner share one runtime-neutral Run Record/reporting owner with schema and output compatibility verified and no inspection rerun introduced.

Shell MainWindow retains only WPF composition and lifecycle responsibilities; smoke, request, recipe-dialog, and layout responsibilities have independent concrete owners and the old ownership is absent.
Workbench and Viewer root partial types are composition facades over independently owned state and execution boundaries, with the former owners no longer retaining moved responsibilities.

State-changing View events route through ViewModel commands; pure presentation conversion and reusable WPF interaction use bounded Converter and Behavior owners while rendering, pointer, docking, and dialog adapters remain in Views.
Current architecture, MVVM rules, dependency direction, verification commands, documentation authority, and binary/vendor policy are documented without duplicating the mutable queue.
Every completed milestone passes proportional focused checks, Release solution build, structure verification, diff hygiene, and any required current Wide/Compact and refreshed R0 validation gates.

milestones.summary: MVVM View, Converter, and Behavior cleanup
Full structural qualification and durable closure

context.summary: The repository already has 12 layered projects and documents partial files as physical boundaries rather than runtime architecture.
ViewModels own state and commands; Views retain dialogs, docking, PropertyGrid, SharpGL, pointer, and screenshot adapters.

Documentation ownership cleanup is complete: the active MVVM plan now documents stable ownership boundaries, dependency direction, DLL/vendor policy, and milestone progress (including M6-M7 completion). `docs/README.md` and `docs/OPENVISIONLAB_3D_NEXT_SESSION_HANDOFF.md` remain owning authorities; this plan adds no queue duplication.

Final closure evidence for this task run: `scripts/verify-code-structure.ps1` passed 49/49 (`reports/code-structure-report-final-m6m7.txt`), Release build passed 0 warnings/0 errors (`release-build-m6m7.txt`), and `git diff --check` returned no issues. The current 49/49 structure guard and 0-warning/0-error Release build pass, but direct source inspection refutes the broad closure: the Viewer View still loads, saves, validates, and executes recipe rules; ToolWorkbenchViewModel remains one 33-file partial type with 15,428 lines, 101 public commands, 50 public events, and direct tool execution; MainWindow retains extensive smoke orchestration; Results and Validation Views still own navigation state; and Tool Lab windows repeat lifecycle code.
